transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

I can’t confirm what “dE” means for this particular LG washer-dryer from the code alone, but with the door shut and the machine refusing to start, the leading possibility is that it is not detecting the door as securely closed. This can be the electrical door interlock, or simply the catch/hinge not engaging fully. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Open the door and check that no washing is trapped in the rubber seal or around the latch area. Check the small hook on the door is not bent or loose, and that the door sits square rather than having dropped on its hinge. Close it firmly until it clicks. A door that only starts when pushed in or lifted points to alignment/catch rather than the electronics. 2. Check whether a padlock/key (child-lock) symbol is lit. If so, turn it off using the button combination shown on the control panel/manual, then try again. 3. With the door closed, switch back on and press Start. Listen for a distinct locking click from the door. No second click makes the door interlock or its wiring more likely; a click followed immediately by the same message can also be an interlock-confirmation or control issue. If the door closes and latches normally but there is no locking click, an engineer is usually the sensible next step: the lock, its connector/loom, and then the control need testing safely. Don’t force the door or try to bypass the lock.
ok tried it. theres a click then nothing, still dE. its got a king size duvet in tho if that matters

The duvet can matter: a king-size duvet can press against the door or stop the catch engaging fully, even when the door appears shut. It would also be too bulky for a reliable spin later on, but it should not normally cause a door error if the door is fully latched. 1. Switch off and unplug the washer-dryer. Remove the duvet completely and check the door closes freely with nothing pushing against the seal.
2. Close it firmly, then try a short rinse/spin or another brief programme with the drum empty. If it starts empty, the issue was the bulky load/door engagement. Wash the duvet only if its care label and the machine’s stated capacity allow it; otherwise use a large commercial machine. The catch/hinge and wiring are the other possibilities, but an engineer should test those rather than bypassing the lock or forcing the door.
ok took the duvet out n tried towels instead, starts fine. so its the duvet then? the door springs back a bit when i shut it with the duvet in, and a corner was squashed in the seal

Yes — the duvet was stopping the door from fully engaging, rather than indicating a failed door lock. The door springing back and the corner being caught in the seal explain the dE message, and the fact it starts with towels suggests the machine itself is able to lock and run. Don’t force that duvet into the drum. If its care label permits machine washing, it needs enough spare room to move freely and the door must close without anything caught in the seal. A king-size duvet is often better done in a suitably sized launderette machine. No part is needed unless it begins showing dE with ordinary loads and a clear, freely closing door.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
